topics.title: Revision of Previous Work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list the main components of a solar PV system.
The students should be able to explain basic wiring connections in solar installations.
The students should be able to discuss real-life solar installation scenarios in Nigeria.

Introduction:
We have learned about solar energy and its components in previous terms. Today, we will revise what we know and discuss how solar technology is used in Nigerian communities.

Content:
Solar components include solar panels, batteries, charge controllers, inverters, and mounting structures. Each part has a specific function: panels convert sunlight to electricity, batteries store energy, controllers regulate charging, inverters convert DC to AC power, and mounting structures hold panels in place.

Wiring in solar systems must be done correctly to prevent energy loss and hazards. We use appropriate wire sizes, proper connections, and safety devices like fuses. In Nigeria, we often see solar systems in rural areas where there is no national grid power, like in villages in Kaduna State.

Real-life scenarios include powering homes, street lights, water pumps, and school computers. For example, in Sokoto, solar panels help power boreholes for clean water during the dry season when there is little rain.

Professional ethics in solar practice means being honest about system capabilities, using quality materials, and ensuring customer safety. Like the market trader who sells genuine goods, a solar technician should provide reliable service.

Class activity:
In groups, students will draw a simple solar system diagram and label all components. Each group will then present their diagram and explain how the system works.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name three main components of a solar PV system.
2. Why is proper wiring important in solar installations?
3. Describe one real-life use of solar technology in Nigeria.
4. How does professional ethics affect solar business in Nigeria?

Summary:
Today we reviewed the key components and wiring of solar systems and discussed their practical applications in Nigerian contexts.

topics.title: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) in Solar Work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify common electrical hazards in solar work.
The students should be able to list the necessary personal protective equipment for solar installation.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper safety procedures when handling solar equipment.

Introduction:
Safety is very important in any technical work, especially with electricity. We have learned about solar components, and now we must learn how to handle them safely to prevent accidents.

Content:
Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) protects workers from harm. In solar work, we face risks like electric shock, falls from heights, cuts from tools, and burns from equipment. These hazards can be prevented by following safety rules.

Common electrical hazards include exposed wires, faulty equipment, and working in wet conditions. In Nigeria during the rainy season, extra care must be taken when installing or maintaining solar systems. Always turn off power before working on electrical components.

Safe handling of panels, batteries, and tools is crucial. Solar panels are heavy and fragile; they should be carried carefully by the edges. Batteries contain acid and can cause burns or explosions if short-circuited. Tools should be properly insulated and used correctly.

Personal protective equipment (PPE) includes safety gloves, goggles, hard hats, non-slip shoes, and insulated clothing. Like the construction workers in Abuja who wear safety gear, solar technicians must wear appropriate PPE for protection.

Class activity:
Students will participate in a safety drill where they demonstrate proper PPE usage and safe handling of solar equipment. They will also inspect provided PPE to identify any damage or defects.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name three electrical hazards in solar work.
2. What PPE should be worn when installing solar panels?
3. Why is battery safety important in solar installations?
4. How does weather affect safety during solar work in Nigeria?

Summary:
Safety is paramount in solar work, and proper use of PPE and safe handling procedures can prevent accidents and injuries.

topics.title: Solar Site Assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify suitable locations for PV systems.
The students should be able to explain factors affecting solar site selection.
The students should be able to perform a basic site assessment using a checklist.

Introduction:
Before installing a solar system, we must carefully choose the right location. This ensures maximum energy production and system longevity. We have learned about solar components, and now we will learn where to place them effectively.

Content:
A suitable location for PV systems receives maximum sunlight throughout the year. In Nigeria, the best locations face south in the northern hemisphere and are free from shading by trees, buildings, or other obstructions. Like farmers who choose fertile land for planting, we choose sunny locations for solar panels.

Factors affecting solar site selection include orientation, shading, tilt angle, and roof strength. Orientation refers to the direction the panels face; in Nigeria, panels should generally face south. Shading reduces energy production, so we avoid areas where shadows fall on panels, especially during peak sun hours.

Tilt angle is the angle at which panels are inclined. In Nigeria, the optimal tilt angle is approximately equal to the latitude of the location. For example, in Lagos (latitude about 6°N), panels should be tilted around 6°. Roof strength is important to support the weight of panels and mounting structures.

Site survey checklist includes measuring available space, noting obstructions, checking structural integrity, and documenting sun path throughout the day. Like the market woman who carefully arranges her goods, we carefully assess the site to plan the installation properly.

Class activity:
Students will perform a basic site assessment around the school. They will use a checklist to measure available space, note potential shading, check structural strength, and document findings with sketches.

Evaluation questions:
1. What direction should solar panels generally face in Nigeria?
2. Name three factors that affect solar site selection.
3. Why is shading important when choosing a solar location?
4. What is the optimal tilt angle for solar panels in Abuja (latitude 9°N)?

Summary:
Proper site assessment is crucial for effective solar installation, as it ensures maximum energy production and system durability.

topics.title: System Installation Procedure
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to describe the step-by-step installation process of a solar PV system.
The students should be able to differentiate between roof and ground mounting installations.
The students should be able to install panels, controllers, inverters, and batteries correctly.

Introduction:
We have learned about solar components and site assessment. Now, we will learn how to install these components to create a working solar system. This process requires careful attention to detail and proper sequencing.

Content:
The installation process follows specific steps for safety and efficiency. First, we prepare the site and install mounting structures. Then we mount the panels, connect wiring, install electrical components, and finally test the system. Like building a house with proper foundation first, we install solar systems in the correct order.

Mounting structures can be roof or ground installations. Roof mounts are common in urban areas where space is limited, like in Lagos apartments. Ground mounts are used where there is available land, such as in rural communities or large compounds. Each type requires different installation techniques and considerations.

Installing panels involves securing them to mounting structures with appropriate brackets and hardware. Panels should be connected according to system voltage requirements-series for higher voltage, parallel for higher current. Like connecting pieces of a puzzle, panel connections must be precise.

Controllers, inverters, and batteries are installed next. The controller manages power flow to batteries, the inverter converts DC to AC power, and batteries store energy for later use. Each component must be properly connected with correct polarity and appropriate wire sizes.

Class activity:
Students will work in groups to install a small off-grid solar lighting system. They will mount panels, connect wiring, install components, and test the system to ensure it functions properly.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the main steps in solar system installation?
2. What is the difference between roof and ground mounting?
3. Why is proper panel connection important in solar installations?
4. What is the function of a charge controller in a solar system?

Summary:
Solar system installation requires careful planning and proper execution of each step to ensure safety, efficiency, and longevity of the system.

topics.title: MID-TERM EXAMINATION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate understanding of weeks 1-4 topics.
The students should be able to apply knowledge in practical solar installation scenarios.

Introduction:
Today we will assess your understanding of the topics covered in the past four weeks through a written examination. This will help me know how well you have grasped the concepts and identify areas that need more attention.

Content:
The examination will cover topics from weeks 1-4, including revision of previous work, occupational health and safety, solar site assessment, and system installation procedure. The questions will test both theoretical knowledge and practical application of concepts.

The examination will consist of multiple choice questions, short answer questions, and a practical component where you will demonstrate installation steps. Like the final examination in the SSCE, this assessment will comprehensively evaluate your understanding of solar photovoltaic installation and maintenance.

Remember to read each question carefully before answering. For practical components, follow safety procedures and show proper handling of equipment. Your performance will reflect your ability to apply classroom learning to real-world situations.

Class activity:
Students will complete the mid-term examination under supervised conditions. The examination will include both written and practical components to assess theoretical knowledge and hands-on skills.

Evaluation questions:
The examination itself serves as the evaluation, with questions covering all topics from weeks 1-4.

Summary:
The mid-term examination provides an opportunity to demonstrate your knowledge and skills in solar photovoltaic installation and maintenance covered in the first four weeks of the term.

topics.title: Maintenance and Servicing of Solar PV Systems corrective Cleaning panels and maintaining batteries Checking electrical connections and components Maintenance schedules and record- keeping Practical: Conducting maintenance on a school solar unit
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to differentiate between preventive and corrective maintenance.
The students should be able to explain proper panel cleaning and battery maintenance procedures.
The students should be able to create a maintenance schedule for a solar system.

Introduction:
Solar systems require regular maintenance to operate efficiently and last longer. We have learned how to install solar systems, and now we will learn how to keep them working properly over time.

Content:
Maintenance of solar PV systems includes both preventive and corrective maintenance. Preventive maintenance involves regular checks and cleaning to prevent problems, like the regular maintenance of a Danfo bus to prevent breakdowns. Corrective maintenance involves fixing problems when they occur, like repairing a faulty inverter.

Cleaning panels is essential because dust, bird droppings, and other debris can block sunlight and reduce efficiency. In Nigeria's dusty environment, panels may need cleaning weekly during the dry season and monthly during the rainy season. Clean panels with soft brushes and clean water, avoiding harsh chemicals that could damage the surface.

Battery maintenance includes checking electrolyte levels (for flooded batteries), cleaning terminals, and ensuring proper ventilation. Like caring for a generator, batteries need regular attention to perform well. In Nigeria's heat, batteries may need more frequent checks as high temperatures can shorten their lifespan.

Checking electrical connections and components involves inspecting wires, fuses, switches, and other parts for wear, damage, or loose connections. Faulty connections can cause energy loss or safety hazards. Regular inspections can identify issues before they become serious problems.

Maintenance schedules should be created based on manufacturer recommendations and local conditions. Daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly tasks should be clearly documented. Like the market trader who keeps records of sales, maintenance records help track system performance and identify patterns of issues.

Class activity:
Students will conduct maintenance on a school solar unit, including cleaning panels, checking battery levels, inspecting connections, and documenting their findings in a maintenance log.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the difference between preventive and corrective maintenance?
2. How often should solar panels be cleaned in Nigeria during the dry season?
3. Why is battery maintenance important in solar systems?
4. What should be included in a maintenance schedule for a solar PV system?

Summary:
Regular maintenance ensures solar systems operate efficiently and have a long lifespan, providing reliable energy for years to come.

topics.title: MID-TERM BREAK Holiday
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to rest and recharge for the second half of the term.

Introduction:
After weeks of hard work learning about solar technology, it is time for a well-deserved break to rest and prepare for the remaining topics in the term.

Content:
This is a holiday period where students should rest, spend time with family, and perhaps observe how solar technology is used in their communities. Like the harmattan season that brings a pause in farming activities, this break allows students to refresh before continuing their studies.

Students are encouraged to use this time to review previous topics and think about how solar energy can benefit their communities. They might notice solar panels in their neighborhoods or discuss renewable energy with family members. This practical observation reinforces classroom learning.

Class activity:
No formal class activity during this holiday period. Students are encouraged to rest and engage in family activities.

Evaluation questions:
No formal evaluation during this holiday period.

Summary:
This mid-term break provides an opportunity to rest and reflect on the knowledge gained so far in the course.

topics.title: Energy Conservation and Meaning Efficiency Ways to reduce power consumption Importance of energy-efficient appliances Role of solar technology in sustainable living Group discussion: Designing an energy- efficient home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the meaning of energy conservation.
The students should be able to list ways to reduce power consumption.
The students should be able to discuss the role of solar technology in sustainable living.

Introduction:
We have learned about solar installation and maintenance. Now, we will explore how to use energy wisely and how solar technology contributes to sustainable living in Nigeria.

Content:
Energy conservation means using less energy while maintaining the same level of service. Like a market woman who carefully manages her goods to avoid waste, we manage energy to avoid unnecessary consumption. This reduces costs and preserves resources for future generations.

Ways to reduce power consumption include using energy-efficient appliances, turning off lights and devices when not in use, improving insulation, and utilizing natural light and ventilation. In Nigerian homes, simple actions like using LED bulbs instead of incandescent ones can significantly reduce electricity consumption.

Energy-efficient appliances use less electricity to perform the same function. When buying appliances, look for energy efficiency ratings. Like choosing a fuel-efficient car, selecting energy-efficient appliances saves money and reduces environmental impact.

Solar technology plays a crucial role in sustainable living by providing clean, renewable energy. In Nigeria, solar power can reduce dependence on fossil fuels and provide electricity in remote areas. Solar water heaters can reduce the need for electric or gas heating, saving energy and money.

Sustainable living means meeting current needs without compromising future generations. Solar technology helps achieve this by providing clean energy that doesn't deplete resources or harm the environment. Like traditional farming practices that worked with nature, sustainable living works with natural systems rather than against them.

Class activity:
Students will participate in a group discussion designing an energy-efficient home. They will consider solar power, energy-efficient appliances, proper insulation, and other conservation methods in their designs.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is energy conservation?
2. Name three ways to reduce power consumption in Nigerian homes.
3. How does solar technology contribute to sustainable living?
4. Why are energy-efficient appliances important in solar power systems?

Summary:
Energy conservation and efficient use of solar technology are essential for sustainable living and reducing environmental impact.

topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify opportunities in the solar energy sector.
The students should be able to list types of solar services.
The students should be able to develop a simple solar business plan.

Introduction:
Solar energy is not just about technology-it's also a business opportunity. We have learned about solar systems, and now we will explore how to turn this knowledge into a sustainable business in Nigeria.

Content:
Understanding solar business opportunities involves recognizing the growing demand for renewable energy in Nigeria. With frequent power outages and the high cost of generators, many Nigerians are turning to solar power. This creates opportunities for installation, maintenance, sales, and consultancy services.

Types of solar services include installation, maintenance, consultancy, and sales. Installation services involve setting up solar systems for homes, businesses, and institutions. Maintenance services ensure existing systems continue working properly. Consultancy services help clients choose appropriate systems for their needs. Sales involve distributing solar products to customers.

Basic costing and quotation writing requires understanding material costs, labor charges, and profit margins. When creating a quotation, list all components, their prices, installation costs, and total amount. Like the tailor who provides a detailed bill for clothes, a solar business should provide clear, accurate quotations to customers.

Building customer relations and trust is essential for business success. This involves honesty about system capabilities, quality workmanship, good communication, and after-sales service. Like the trusted neighborhood mechanic who consistently provides reliable service, a solar business builds reputation through consistent quality.

A simple business plan should include business name, target market, services offered, pricing strategy, marketing approach, and financial projections. Even small solar businesses benefit from planning, like the small-scale farmer who plans planting and harvesting seasons for better yields.

Class activity:
Students will develop a simple solar business plan, including business name, target market, services offered, pricing, and marketing approach. They will present their plans to the class for feedback.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name three opportunities in the solar energy sector in Nigeria.
2. What are the main types of solar services?
3. Why is customer trust important in solar business?
4. What should be included in a simple solar business plan?

Summary:
The solar energy sector offers various business opportunities that can provide sustainable income while contributing to Nigeria's renewable energy development.
